This author has some good points, but I don't think its fair to just say "anytime the bell curve shifts to the left these people take over society and destroy it". You need real, empirical evidence to back up a statement like that. Otherwise its just spewing conjecture.

There are plenty of examples. The French Revolution is often fetishized by the left - in fact, it created the whole concept of left vs. right to begin with - but it led to a severe vicious cycle of political instability that France didn't recover from until at least the 1960s. For another example, look at the failure of the Soviet Union or North Korea or Venezuela or Greece.

Extreme, unfettered leftism destroys countries by making envy and jealousy between arbitrary factions the focal point of society, producing mediocrity, destroying the economy and enabling authoritarian regimes to sieze power.

I'm glad that you support the arguments and sentiments of the author (I do too), but there is no empirical evidence for any of this. Thus, it is still just conjecture.

For this statement and others like it to be accepted, we need concrete FACTS from a reliable source. You can't just say "look at the failure of the Soviet Union or North Korea".

It's an empirical fact that post-Revolution France cycled through dictators, monarchs, republics and parliaments - a process that was rife with violent uprisings and coup d'etats - until finally settling on their current system of government (The Fifth Republic) in 1958. That much instability isn't good for any nation.

It's an empirical fact that the Soviet Union hyperinflated its currency (reaching a whopping 1240% percent - yes, that's one thousand two hundred and forty - by 1992), destroyed its domestic agricultural sector by exiling the most productive farmers to Siberia and collectivizing and nationalizing farmland, pumped out shoddy products that were obsolete before they even rolled off the assembly line, failed to rationally allocate resources because of their strict regimen of central planning and price controls, and bankrupted itself by trying to keep up with Reagan's military spending. All this was done in the name of leftism, Marxism and equality of outcome.

It's an empirical fact that Venezuela suffers from severe shortages of basic necessities (such as toilet paper and food) due to central planning, is on the brink of hyperinflation, and will inevitably end up like Weimar Germany. Like with the Soviet Union, this is the direct result of radical leftist leaders taking control with zero competition or alternative options.

It's an empirical fact that Greece has had to be bailed out three times in the last five years, has teetered on the edge of bankruptcy for the past year, and is up to its eyeballs in debt that can never realistically be paid off in our lifetime. As usual, the leftists in charge spent decades promising everything for free - including pie-in-the-sky retirement ages and pension plans - in order to buy votes and remain in power, and they soon discovered that there really were limits to other people's money.

As for North Korea - the difference between their unfettered leftism and South Korea's capitalism can literally be seen from space.

Fine- you have empirical facts about cherry-picked countries and why each of them crumbled. Correlation doesn't equal causation.

What the author doesn't have is a causal argument, backed with empirical evidence, that takes the sentence "anytime the bell curve shifts to the left these people take over society and destroy it" and turns it into a causal argument. What you need is empirical evidence that supports the causal mechanism (the bell curve shifting to the left causes the destruction of society), and can be used to predict future social collapses. His argument is pure conjecture.

Some examples of the kind of evidence the author (or you) needs to turn this into an argument:

1) How far does the bell curve need to shift to the left to cause the collapse of a society?

2) Is there any evidence that disproves your argument? If even ONE country survives with a population whose ideological bell curve has shifted past your theorized point in question 1, your argument is wrong.

3) Check for control variables, e.g. "Can nations with agricultural economies survive more of a leftist shift than nations with industrial economies?"

4) Spurious Correlations- All the countries you listed were recent survivors of devastating wars during the time periods you mentioned. Who is to say that some other variable didn't cause the social collapse?
